title: Elevated nitrogen deposition protects an invasive plant from herbivory through altering leaf volatile‐mediated tritrophic interactions
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Atmospheric nitrogen deposition disrupts plant–herbivore interactions, but its impact on leaf volatile organic compounds (VOCs)-mediated multi-trophic herbivore resistance remains unclear within the context of plant invasion. In this study, we initially investigated the differences in leaf feeding damage and number of eggs laid by herbivores between the invasive weed Alternanthera philoxeroides and its native congener, Alternanthera sessilis, in different terrestrial habitats that experienced various levels of atmospheric nitrogen deposition. Furthermore, we compared the quantity and composition of leaf constitutive plant volatiles (CPVs) and herbivore-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) between the two plant species under simulated nitrogen deposition and tested olfactory and oviposition responses of herbivores and natural enemies at multi-trophic levels. Field surveys showed less consumed leaf area and fewer herbivore eggs laid on A. philoxeroides than on A. sessilis in terrestrial habitats experiencing high levels of atmospheric nitrogen deposition. Laboratory bioassays revealed that simulated nitrogen deposition increased the emission and altered the composition of both CPVs and HIPVs in A. philoxeroides compared with A. sessilis. These changes reduced its attractiveness to specialist and generalist herbivores while enhancing its appeal to predatory beetles. Methyl salicylate was identified as the key compound driving these changes in insect behaviours, highlighting its critical role in mediating plant–insect interactions in A. philoxeroides under elevated nitrogen deposition. Synthesis. These findings suggest that leaf VOC-mediated multi-trophic interactions may facilitate A. philoxeroides invasion success under elevated atmospheric nitrogen deposition in this specific study system, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding how nitrogen enrichment could influence plant–herbivore–predator interactions.

摘要

大气氮沉降会干扰植物–植食性昆虫的相互作用，但其在植物入侵背景下对叶片挥发性有机化合物介导的多营养级抗虫性的影响仍不清楚。 本研究首先调查了在不同大气氮沉降水平的陆生生境中，入侵杂草空心莲子草与其本土同属种莲子草在叶片取食损伤程度和植食性昆虫产卵数量上的差异。随后，我们比较了模拟氮沉降条件下两种植物的叶片组成型植物挥发物和虫害诱导型植物挥发物的数量与组成，并测试了多营养级水平上植食性昆虫和天敌的嗅觉与产卵反应。 野外调查表明，在大气氮沉降水平较高的陆生生境中，与莲子草相比，空心莲子草被取食的叶面积更小、植食性昆虫在其上产卵数量更少。室内生物测定显示，与莲子草相比，模拟氮沉降增加了空心莲子草叶片组成型和虫害诱导型挥发物的释放量并改变了其组成。这些变化降低了其对专食性和广食性植食性昆虫的吸引力，同时增强了其对捕食性甲虫的吸引力。水杨酸甲酯被鉴定为驱动这些昆虫行为变化的关键化合物，凸显了其在模拟氮沉降条件下空心莲子草–昆虫相互作用中的关键介导作用。 综合而言，这些发现表明，在该特定研究系统中，叶片挥发物介导的多营养级相互作用可能促进了高氮沉降条件下空心莲子草的入侵成功，为理解氮富集如何影响植物–植食性昆虫–捕食者相互作用提供了机制基础。
